pages.quiz:
ENGLISH ACTIVITIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #8
====

GRADE: Grade 1
SUBJECT: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. where is the library
   B. Where is the library?
   C. Where is the library
   D. Where is the Library

2. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. happiness
   B. run
   C. blue
   D. quickly

3. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. Only a describing word
   C. Only an action
   D. A person, place, thing, or idea

4. When practising Attentive listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Attentive listening.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Attentive listening.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Attentive listening.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive listening.

5. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. No full stops
   B. Only one word repeated
   C. Many unrelated topics with no link
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

6. When practising Handwriting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Handwriting.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Handwriting.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Handwriting.

7. When practising Connected text and fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Connected text and fluency.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Connected text and fluency.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Connected text and fluency.

8. When practising Language Welcome and, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Language Welcome and.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Welcome and.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Language Welcome and.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Language Welcome and.

9. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goed
   B. going
   C. goes
   D. went

10. When practising Phonics, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Phonics.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonics.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Phonics.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Phonics.

11. When practising Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Comprehension.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Comprehension.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Comprehension.

12. When practising Pre-Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Pre-Writing.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Pre-Writing.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre-Writing.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Pre-Writing.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Pre Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Phonics and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Word Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Connected text and fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — Where is the library?

2. B — run

3. D — A person, place, thing, or idea

4. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive listening.

5. D — One main idea with supporting sentences

6. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.

7. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.

8. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Welcome and.

9. D — went

10. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonics.

11. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.

12. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre-Writing.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Pre Reading; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Phonics; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Word Reading; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Connected text and fluency; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
